key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings become denser and more corrosion-resistant when droplets flatten well during deposition, while higher humidity lowers friction and wear through tribochemical effects.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray parameters and controlling porosity can improve the long-term durability of steel protection coatings used in corrosive and humid service environments.
method: Detonation spray Fe-based amorphous coatings onto Q235 carbon steel under different spraying parameters
Compare coating microstructure, porosity, corrosion resistance, and tribological behavior
Test wear against Si3N4 balls under different humidity conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic corrosion and tribology testing and links higher droplet circularity/expansion to denser coatings, lower porosity to better long-term corrosion resistance, and increasing humidity to reduced friction coefficient and wear rate.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on spray-induced porosity and environmental humidity, so the coating may need tight process control and environment-specific validation before deployment.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
